Q17579784.summary: On the face of this marble capital for a pair of columns, the crowned Virgin sits frontally within a beaded mandorla, holding before her the Christ Child, who has a cross-nimbus and a book. The winged creatures of the evangelists press around the mandorla, honouring the Child as the incarnate Word. Another face of the capital shows the Crucifixion, with the lance thrust into Christ's side.
facts: The capital comes from the abbey of Saint-Pons-de-Thomières and entered the Musée des Augustins by 1865.
The museum describes the Christ Child with a cross-nimbus and a book, and the Virgin seated on a zoomorphic stool.
It is about 39 cm high and 50 cm wide.
Q17579784.notes: The museum dates it to the 12th century (1101–1200); Wikidata says 11th. Only the Virgin-and-Child face is shown in this image.

cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: Against a purple ground, a figure stripped to the waist stands bound to a column while two men swing scourges at him from either side. The verse above reads 'they gnashed upon me with their teeth' and speaks of mockery and scorn, which the painter applied to the scourging of Christ.
facts: The Stuttgart Psalter was made around 820–830 at the abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés near Paris; its 168 leaves contain the psalms with 316 coloured miniatures set between the verses they illustrate.
Its pictures interpret the psalms literally, historically or — very often — Christologically, as prophecies of the life of Christ.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature. The face of the bound figure is hidden by the column; identification as Christ follows the manuscript's Christological reading of this psalm.
